Find the $x$-intercepts of the circle $(x+4)^{2}+{y}^{2}=25,$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
We must have $y=0$ at the $x$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =25 \\ (x+4)^{2}+{0}^{2} & =25 \\ (x+4)^{2} & =25 \\ x+4 & =\pm \sqrt{25} \\ x+4 & =\pm 5 \\ x & =-4\pm 5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts occur at the points $(-9,0)$ and $(1,0).$

Find the $x$-intercepts of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-8x+6y+15=0,$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
We must have $y=0$ at the $x$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-8x+6y+15 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+{0}^{2}-8x+6\cdot 0+15 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-8x+15 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this equation by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-8x+16+15 & =0+16 \\ (x-4)^{2}+15 & =16 \\ (x-4)^{2} & =1 \\ x-4 & =\pm 1 \\ x & =4\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts occur at the points $(3,0)$ and $(5,0).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-x+4y & =5 \\ {0}^{2}+{y}^{2}-0+4y & =5 \\ {y}^{2}+4y & =5\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this equation by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+4y+4 & =5+4 \\ (y+2)^{2} & =9 \\ y+2 & =\pm 3 \\ y & =-2\pm 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $y$-intercepts occur at the points $(0,-5)$ and $(0,1),$ as shown below.

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Circle Does Not Intersect an Axis
questions.worked_solution:
When the circle intercepts the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$

So, we need to substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve the resulting equation for $y$, if possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2}+(y+4)^{2} & =9 \\ (0-4)^{2}+(y+4)^{2} & =9 \\ 16+(y+4)^{2} & =9 \\ (y+4)^{2} & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(y+4)^{2}\ge 0$ for all values of $y,$ there is no $y$ such that $(y+4)^{2}=-7.$ Therefore, the circle does not intercept the $y$-axis at any point, as shown below.

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We must have $x = 0$ at the $y$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $x = 0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-2y & =8 \\ (0)^{2}+{y}^{2}+2(0)-2y & =8 \\ {y}^{2}-2y & =8\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this equation by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-2y+1 & =8+1 \\ (y-1)^{2} & =9 \\ y-1 & =\pm 3 \\ y & =1\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercepts occur at  $(0,-2)$ and $(0,4).$
